import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Normality of mathematical constants

Despite extensive empirical evidence—billions of digits have been computed for $\pi$,
$e$, and $\sqrt{2}$, all showing near-uniform digit distribution—it is an open problem
whether any of the classical constants $\pi$, $e$, $\sqrt{2}$, $\ln 2$, or $\varphi$ is
normal in any base.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia (Normal number)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_number)
* [Wikipedia (Pi)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pi)
-/

open Real

namespace NormalNumber

/--
$\pi$ is normal in base 10.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem pi_normal_base_ten : IsNormalInBase 10 π := by
  sorry

end NormalNumber

findings.description: The conclusion `IsNormalInBase 10 π` asserts only simple normality in base 10. The imported definition `NormalNumber.IsNormalInBase` (FormalConjecturesForMathlib/NumberTheory/NormalNumber.lean, lines 63–69) quantifies over individual digits `d < b` and requires each to have limiting frequency `1/b`; it never quantifies over longer digit blocks. Full base-10 normality also requires every length-m block to have frequency 10^(-m). These properties are not equivalent: in /workspace/review/witness.lean, Lean verifies that x = 123456789/9999999999 = 0.01234567890123456789… satisfies `IsNormalInBase 10 x`, while its `00`-block frequency cannot tend to 1/100 because that block never occurs. Thus the theorem omits a substantive part of the conjecture.
findings.source_evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_number, introduction and Definitions: single-digit frequency 1/b defines 'simply normal'; 'normal in base b' requires, for every positive integer n, all strings n digits long to have density b^(-n). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pi#Irrationality_and_normality likewise defines normality using 'all possible sequences of digits (of any given length)' and states the conjecture that π is normal.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the existing shared predicate to `IsSimplyNormalInBase` and define `IsNormalInBase` using all nonempty finite digit blocks, then retain the theorem with that corrected predicate. Equivalently, with the current predicate unchanged, strengthen the conclusion to `∀ m : ℕ, 0 < m → IsNormalInBase (10 ^ m) π`: simple normality in every positive power of base 10 is equivalent to full base-10 normality, as the source's Properties section states.

review.notes: Checked the file's sole declaration and its imported definitions. /workspace/review/scratch.lean checks unfolding, zero-indexed digit extraction, terminating decimals, and the n = 0 frequency. That initial division-by-zero value does not affect the limit atTop on ℕ; invalid bases are unreachable in this fixed-base theorem. /workspace/review/witness.lean compiles and proves the counterexample's single-digit normality and failure of uniform 00-block frequency; both proofs' axiom lists exclude sorryAx. Both cited sources still describe π's normality as open. The shared-definition defect is reported once against the theorem under review.

submission.summary: Strengthened the theorem to require simple normality in every base 10^m for positive integers m, which is equivalent to full base-10 normality. Updated its docstring without changing shared definitions or other files. The required Lean compile reports no errors and only the permitted `sorry` warning.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Normality of mathematical constants

Despite extensive empirical evidence—billions of digits have been computed for $\pi$,
$e$, and $\sqrt{2}$, all showing near-uniform digit distribution—it is an open problem
whether any of the classical constants $\pi$, $e$, $\sqrt{2}$, $\ln 2$, or $\varphi$ is
normal in any base.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia (Normal number)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_number)
* [Wikipedia (Pi)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pi)
-/

open Real

namespace NormalNumber

/--
$\pi$ is normal in base 10. Equivalently, it is simply normal in base $10^m$
for every positive integer $m$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem pi_normal_base_ten :
    ∀ m : ℕ, 0 < m → IsNormalInBase (10 ^ m) π := by
  sorry

end NormalNumber
